Subject: Re: Fwd: Latency SLO request for upcoming StellarTech rollout

Thanks for the ping. Quick baseline assessment after an initial sim (see attached CSV):
- With Redwood Dedicated (pinned GPUs), warm instances, and KV cache priming we can hit p95 ~42-48ms for short prompts (~<=120 tokens) at moderate concurrency (<=150 concurrent requests across pool) using the optimized attention kernels.
- Risk factors: long prompts (>300 tokens), heavy multimodal payloads, sudden concurrency spikes beyond expected ramp, and cold starts. Those increase p95 into the 70-120ms range.
- Operational needs: dedicated pool sized for sustained peak (I'd budget for ~2x expected peak to preserve headroom), proactive KV cache priming during canary/peak windows, and an automated fallback to a slightly larger model variant (same architecture, higher latency) if health signals cross thresholds.

Requirements to offer a contractual sub-50ms p95:
1) Customer must run on a Dedicated cluster with reserved capacity (we can't promise on shared hosted API).
2) We need a short canary period (1 week) to tune caching and routing.
3) Observability hooks + log retention for p95 calculation (we need explicit approval for token-level sampling retention).

I'll attach the latency-sim-results.csv with the scenario matrix. Next steps: confirm the expected prompt length distribution and peak concurrency windows from StellarTech, and decide on the size of the reserved pool.

- Marissa
Director, Product & Infra
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Latency SLO request for upcoming StellarTech rollout

Appreciate the assessment. Commercial perspective / proposed guardrails:
- We can offer a conditional SLA for sub-50ms p95 provided the technical pre-reqs Marissa listed are met (Dedicated reserved pool + canary week + telemetry).
- Proposed commercial terms: 12-month reserved commitment for the Dedicated pool sized for 2x peak with a 10% discount on list + an operational credit: if monthly p95 >65ms for more than two triggered windows, StellarTech receives a 30% credit on that month's Dedicated fee.
- We should avoid hard-dollar penalties; credits aligned to remedial ops effort are preferable. Legal will want explicit measurement methodology, windowing rules, and allowed maintenance windows.

Questions for product: can we automate the fallback behavior Marissa suggested (model variant routing + throttled queuing) so ops burden is minimized? Also, what's the effort to add the p95 calculation into the Console and expose a per-route metric for the customer?

If agreed, I'll draft the SLA clause and a short term sheet MVP and loop Legal & Finance. We should also scope an internal ops runbook (MOP) that Marissa or Marcus can review.

- Kimberly
Head of Sales, Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Latency SLO request for upcoming StellarTech rollout -- proposed path

Emily — thanks for the quick request and context. Aligning internal next steps and proposed path below:

What we can offer (conditional):
- A contracted sub-50ms p95 for US region traffic on Redwood Dedicated with reserved capacity sized to customer peak (we recommend sizing to 2x expected peak to provide headroom).
- One-week canary and tuning window pre-production where both teams validate p95 measurements.
- Observability hooks and per-route p95 exposure in Redwood Console (we will surface token-sampled metrics; final data retention to be agreed).
- Operational fallback: automatic routing to a slightly higher-latency model variant + throttled queuing if health thresholds are met (to preserve correctness).

Commercial ask / mitigations:
- 12-month Dedicated commitment (discounted) + operational credits (proposed: 30% credit if monthly p95 >65ms for two or more windows, subject to exclusions).

Attachments: proposed MOP and the sim results from product (for your review).

Please confirm:
1) Timeline — can you confirm a July 1 go-live hard date or flexibility to shift to July 8 if tuning requires it?
2) Prompt distribution — Emily, can you share a representative sample or stats for token lengths and a peak concurrency window?

If you confirm the timeline, Kimberly will draft a short SLA clause and finance will prepare a term sheet. Marissa/Marcus will scope the Dedicated pool and runbook. Target internal signoff 6/21 so we can circulate to Legal.

--
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
